name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
      - LICENSE
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
      - LICENSE

permissions:
  contents: read

# A push supersedes the runs before it on a pull request: the newest commit's
# run covers theirs. On main a run that started finishes, so that main has a
# history to tell whether a test that fails on a pull request fails without
# it; at most the newest commit waits behind it, and GitHub cancels the older
# ones waiting. A release commit runs on its own, so that it is neither queued
# behind nor canceled by others, as its tag waits for its run.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}${{ startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'Release ') && format('-{0}', github.sha) || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  test:
    name: ${{ matrix.name }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      # GStreamer's plugins play the videos of ui/video's tests.
      LINUX_PACKAGES: libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 libayatana-appindicator3-1 xvfb xauth dbus-x11 libgl1-mesa-dri libglx-mesa0 libegl-mesa0 gstreamer1.0-plugins-base gstreamer1.0-plugins-good gstreamer1.0-libav
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { name: macOS, os: macos-latest }
          - { name: Linux, os: ubuntu-latest }
          - { name: Windows, os: windows-latest }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
      # Ubuntu's mirrors are slow now and then (9 minutes for these packages
      # once), so the packages are kept in the Actions cache, under a key of
      # the files apt would download for them.
      - name: List the packages for WebKitGTK and a virtual display
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        id: apt
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          debs=$(apt-get install --print-uris -qq -y --no-install-recommends $LINUX_PACKAGES | awk '{print $2}' | sort | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
          echo "prefix=apt-$ImageOS-${{ runner.arch }}-" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "key=apt-$ImageOS-${{ runner.arch }}-$debs" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Restore the packages
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        id: apt-cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/apt-archives
          key: ${{ steps.apt.outputs.key }}
          restore-keys: ${{ steps.apt.outputs.prefix }}
      - name: Install WebKitGTK and a virtual display
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          mkdir -p ~/.cache/apt-archives/partial
          apt="-o Dir::Cache::Archives=$HOME/.cache/apt-archives -o APT::Sandbox::User=root"
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends $apt $LINUX_PACKAGES
          # Drops what a restored older cache has that the mirror no longer does.
          sudo apt-get autoclean $apt
          sudo chown -R "$USER" ~/.cache/apt-archives
      - name: Save the packages
        if: runner.os == 'Linux' && steps.apt-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/apt-archives
          key: ${{ steps.apt.outputs.key }}
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Build the JavaScript packages
        run: bun run build
      - name: Build and vet every platform
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          for os in darwin linux windows; do
            GOOS=$os go build ./...
            GOOS=$os go vet ./...
            # Production builds leave the inspector of native UI out.
            GOOS=$os go vet -tags mygo_noinspector ./...
          done
          GOOS=freebsd go build ./...
          # 32-bit Windows and Linux have no backend, but compile.
          GOOS=windows GOARCH=386 go build ./...
          GOOS=linux GOARCH=386 go build ./...
          # Browsers run native UI; the CLI is for desktops.
          export GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm
          go build $(go list -f '{{if .GoFiles}}{{.ImportPath}}{{end}}' ./... | grep -v /cmd/mygo)
          go vet $(go list ./... | grep -v /cmd/mygo)
          go test -exec "$(go env GOROOT)/lib/wasm/go_js_wasm_exec" ./internal/web ./internal/gpu/gl
          # The canvas engine's line breaking, with a canvas of its test's.
          go test -exec "$(go env GOROOT)/lib/wasm/go_js_wasm_exec" -run 'TestCanvas|TestKeepWords' ./internal/text
      # The plugins' tests load the native libraries their mygo-plugin.json
      # pins, and on Windows the installer tests run the NSIS that
      # internal/nsis pins, all of which they download into the user's cache
      # when it lacks them. Downloading them here, before the tests, and
      # keeping them in the Actions cache under a key of what pins them,
      # keeps the tests off the network and its hosts' passing failures.
      - name: Restore the downloads of the tests
        id: downloads
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v6
        with:
          path: |
            ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '~/AppData/Local' || runner.os == 'macOS' && '~/Library/Caches' || '~/.cache' }}/mygo/natives
            ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '~/AppData/Local' || runner.os == 'macOS' && '~/Library/Caches' || '~/.cache' }}/mygo/nsis-*
          key: downloads-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('plugins/*/mygo-plugin.json', 'internal/nsis/nsis.go') }}
      - name: Download what the tests need
        run: go run ./internal/prefetch
      - name: Save the downloads of the tests
        if: steps.downloads.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v6
        with:
          path: |
            ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '~/AppData/Local' || runner.os == 'macOS' && '~/Library/Caches' || '~/.cache' }}/mygo/natives
            ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '~/AppData/Local' || runner.os == 'macOS' && '~/Library/Caches' || '~/.cache' }}/mygo/nsis-*
          key: ${{ steps.downloads.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
      # cmd/mygo builds and packages apps, which takes the macOS runners
      # about six minutes and, on a slow one beside the other packages,
      # past go test's ten: the same tests, more time.
      - run: go test -timeout ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' && '20m' || '10m' }} ./...
      - name: Test without the inspector, as production builds
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: go test -tags mygo_noinspector ./ui .
      - run: bun run test
      - run: bun run typecheck
      - name: GUI tests
        if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        env:
          MYGO_E2E: 1
        run: go test ./internal/e2e
      - name: GUI tests
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        env:
          MYGO_E2E: 1
          XDG_DATA_HOME: ${{ runner.temp }}/xdg-data
          XDG_CONFIG_HOME: ${{ runner.temp }}/xdg-config
        run: xvfb-run -a dbus-run-session -- go test ./internal/e2e
      # Runners have no GPU, so native UI draws on the CPU above; MYGO_GPU=1
      # draws it with OpenGL all the same, on Mesa's llvmpipe.
      - name: GUI tests of native UI drawn with OpenGL
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        env:
          MYGO_E2E: 1
          MYGO_GPU: 1
        run: xvfb-run -a dbus-run-session -- go test -run 'TestContentWindow' ./internal/e2e

  # Windows on ARM64, which no machine of the maintainers runs: DirectWrite's
  # methods taking floats go through purego, which sets the floating point
  # registers syscall leaves alone there, and Direct3D 11 draws native UI.
  # The JavaScript packages are the same everywhere, so Bun is left out.
  windows-arm64:
    name: Windows ARM64
    runs-on: windows-11-arm
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      # As in the job above.
      - name: Restore the downloads of the tests
        id: downloads
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v6
        with:
          path: |
            ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '~/AppData/Local' || runner.os == 'macOS' && '~/Library/Caches' || '~/.cache' }}/mygo/natives
            ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '~/AppData/Local' || runner.os == 'macOS' && '~/Library/Caches' || '~/.cache' }}/mygo/nsis-*
          key: downloads-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('plugins/*/mygo-plugin.json', 'internal/nsis/nsis.go') }}
      - name: Download what the tests need
        run: go run ./internal/prefetch
      - name: Save the downloads of the tests
        if: steps.downloads.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v6
        with:
          path: |
            ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '~/AppData/Local' || runner.os == 'macOS' && '~/Library/Caches' || '~/.cache' }}/mygo/natives
            ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '~/AppData/Local' || runner.os == 'macOS' && '~/Library/Caches' || '~/.cache' }}/mygo/nsis-*
          key: ${{ steps.downloads.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
      - run: go test ./...
      - name: Test without the inspector, as production builds
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: go test -tags mygo_noinspector ./ui .
      - name: GUI tests of native UI
        env:
          MYGO_E2E: 1
        run: go test -run 'TestContentWindow' ./internal/e2e

# permissionflow

The permissions the system keeps for the user to give, such as
Accessibility, Screen Recording and the microphone, for
[MyGo](https://github.com/egoist/mygo) apps: checked, asked for with the
system's prompt, and a guide to System Settings, where a panel under its
window holds the app to drag into the list, as
[PermissionFlow](https://github.com/jaywcjlove/PermissionFlow) does for
Swift apps. macOS and Windows; it is all Go.

```go
import "github.com/egoist/mygo/plugins/permissionflow"

st, err := permissionflow.Check(permissionflow.Accessibility)
if err == nil && st != permissionflow.Granted {
	st, err = permissionflow.Guide(ctx, permissionflow.Accessibility, permissionflow.GuideOptions{})
}
```

See [the documentation](../../docs/plugins/permissionflow.md), and
`examples/permissionflow`. It follows PermissionFlow (MIT, © 小弟调调;
see [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md)).

import { afterEach, expect, test } from "bun:test"
import fs from "node:fs/promises"
import os from "node:os"
import path from "node:path"
import { docsAssets } from "../website/llms"
import { rewriteHref } from "../website/src/lib/markdown-source"

const temporary: string[] = []
afterEach(async () => {
  for (const dir of temporary.splice(0)) await fs.rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })
})

test("publishes every doc, with nested README paths and no repository-only instructions", async () => {
  const repo = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "mygo-llms-"))
  temporary.push(repo)
  await fs.mkdir(path.join(repo, "docs/ui"), { recursive: true })
  await fs.mkdir(path.join(repo, "docs/plugins"), { recursive: true })
  const sources = {
    "README.md": "# Introduction\n\nOverview.\n\n[Native UI](ui/README.md)\n",
    "ui/README.md": "# Native UI\n\nNative overview.\n\n[Home](../README.md)\n",
    "plugins/fetch.md": `# Fetch

Fetch data.

[UI](../ui/README.md#input) and [Go file](../../app.go).
[External](https://example.com) and [Local](#options).
[Reference][ui]

[ui]: ../ui/README.md?view=all#input

<!-- repository-only:start -->

## Private instructions

Never publish this.

<!-- repository-only:end -->

## Options

| Option | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Method | GET |

~~~html
<!-- repository-only:start -->
This is a code example.
<!-- repository-only:end -->
~~~
`,
  }
  for (const [file, source] of Object.entries(sources)) await fs.writeFile(path.join(repo, "docs", file), source)
  const assets = await docsAssets(repo)
  expect([...assets.keys()]).toEqual(["/docs.md", "/docs/plugins/fetch.md", "/docs/ui.md", "/llms.txt", "/llms-full.txt"])
  const index = assets.get("/llms.txt")!
  expect(index).toStartWith("# MyGo\n\n> ")
  for (const file of ["/docs.md", "/docs/plugins/fetch.md", "/docs/ui.md"]) {
    expect(index).toContain(`https://mygo.egoist.dev${file}`)
    expect(assets.get("/llms-full.txt")).toContain(assets.get(file)!.trimEnd())
  }
  const fetch = assets.get("/docs/plugins/fetch.md")!
  expect(fetch).toContain("https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui.md#input")
  expect(fetch).toContain("https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/ui.md?view=all#input")
  expect(fetch).toContain("https://github.com/egoist/mygo/blob/main/app.go")
  expect(fetch).toContain("[External](https://example.com)")
  expect(fetch).toContain("[Local](#options)")
  expect(fetch).toContain("| Method | GET")
  expect(fetch).toContain("```html\n<!-- repository-only:start -->\nThis is a code example.")
  for (const text of assets.values()) {
    expect(text).not.toContain("Private instructions")
    expect(text).not.toContain("Never publish this")
  }
  expect(assets.get("/docs/ui.md")).toContain("https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs.md")

  // The dev server and subsequent builds read the current source each time.
  await fs.writeFile(path.join(repo, "docs/new.md"), "# New page\n\nNew content.\n")
  expect((await docsAssets(repo)).get("/llms.txt")).toContain("[New page](https://mygo.egoist.dev/docs/new.md)")
})

test("shared link rules keep HTML docs URLs and repository links intact", () => {
  const links = { docsDir: "/repo/docs", repoDir: "/repo", repoUrl: "https://github.com/egoist/mygo" }
  const file = "/repo/docs/ui/button.md"
  expect(rewriteHref("README.md#views", file, links)).toBe("/docs/ui#views")
  expect(rewriteHref("../README.md", file, links)).toBe("/docs")
  expect(rewriteHref("../../ui/button.go", file, links)).toBe("https://github.com/egoist/mygo/blob/main/ui/button.go")
  expect(rewriteHref("../../examples", file, links)).toBe("https://github.com/egoist/mygo/tree/main/examples")
  for (const href of ["#input", "/docs/ui", "https://example.com", "//example.com", "mailto:hello@example.com"]) {
    expect(rewriteHref(href, file, links)).toBe(href)
  }
})

# MyGo documentation

MyGo builds desktop apps in Go. Each window shows one of two kinds of
interface, and one app can have windows of both:

- **A web page**, in the webview of the operating system (WKWebView on
  macOS, WebKitGTK on Linux, WebView2 on Windows) instead of a bundled
  browser. The frontend is HTML, CSS and JavaScript built with any tools,
  and calls your Go code through a TypeScript client that MyGo generates
  from it, with the types of your Go structs and the documentation of your
  methods.
- **Native UI**, which MyGo draws itself on the GPU, written in Go alone
  with package `ui`: there is no HTML, no JavaScript and no webview to
  start, so the window opens at once and takes little memory.

Windows of both kinds share the window options and events, the menus and
the desktop APIs, and the app is a single Go program of a few megabytes.

A window with a web page, whose frontend calls a Go service:

```go
type Greeter struct{}

// Greet returns a greeting.
func (Greeter) Greet(name string) string { return "Hello, " + name }

func main() {
	mygo.Bind(Greeter{})
	mygo.App.WhenReady(func() {
		mygo.NewWindow(mygo.WindowOptions{Title: "Hello", URL: "/"})
	})
	if err := mygo.App.Run(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

```ts
import { Greeter } from "./mygo"; // generated

document.body.textContent = await Greeter.greet("Ada");
```

A window with native UI, whose view is a Go function of the app's state:

```go
type counter struct{ n int }

func (s *counter) view(c *ui.Context) {
	ui.Column(c).Fill().Center().Gap(12).Children(func() {
		ui.Text(c, fmt.Sprint(s.n)).FontSize(40).Bold()
		if ui.PrimaryButton(c, "Increment").Clicked() {
			s.n++
		}
	})
}

func main() {
	s := &counter{}
	mygo.App.WhenReady(func() {
		mygo.NewWindow(mygo.WindowOptions{
			Title:   "Counter",
			Content: ui.View(s.view),
		})
	})
	if err := mygo.App.Run(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

Web pages suit rich documents, existing web code and what only a browser
does; native UI suits tools, settings, inspectors and utilities, and apps
that must start instantly.

## Getting started

- [Getting started](getting-started.md): install the tools, then create,
  develop and build an app, with native UI or a web frontend.

## Building the app

What every app has, whether its windows show native UI or web pages.

- [Windows](windows.md): creating and arranging windows of both kinds,
  their events, and what windows showing web pages do with them:
  navigation, downloads, permissions, printing.
- [The application](app.md): the lifecycle, quitting, a single instance,
  deep links, file associations, recent documents, starting at login,
  well-known directories, the jump list, drawing web pages on Linux,
  browsing data, cookies and sessions.
- [Menus and the tray](menus.md): application, context and Dock menus,
  keyboard shortcuts and tray icons.
- [Documents](documents.md): document-based apps, a window per file, with
  the File menu, autosave, recovery after a crash, asking to save before
  closing and quitting, and files changed by other apps.
- [Languages](i18n.md): the app's messages in the languages it ships,
  with catalogs of ICU messages, typed Go and TypeScript functions, plural
  forms, MyGo's own strings, and pseudo locales to test layouts.
- [Desktop APIs](native.md): dialogs, notifications, the clipboard, the
  shell, displays, dark mode, power, the network status, secrets, watching
  files and global shortcuts.
- [Clipboard and drag data](data-transfer.md): multiple representations,
  file lists, custom formats, lazy providers, and clipboard persistence.
- [Audio](audio.md): sound effects, streamed music and sound an app makes
  itself, mixed in Go, with WAV, Ogg Vorbis and MP3.
- [Launchers](launchers.md): apps in the manner of Spotlight and Raycast,
  summoned by a shortcut over every app, which find and open the apps
  installed.

## Native UI

[Native UI](ui/README.md) has documentation of its own: guides to views,
layout, input, navigation and accessibility, and a page for each of its
components, from buttons to tables.

## Web pages

- [The frontend](frontend.md): how pages load during development and in
  builds, the `mygo-runtime` package, custom protocols, custom title bars
  and dropped files.
- [Calling Go from the frontend](bindings.md): bound services, channels,
  typed events and the generated TypeScript client.
- [Plugins](plugins.md): features that come in a Go package and an npm
  package, such as the official plugins, and writing your own.

## Shipping

- [Building and distributing](distribution.md): packaged apps for macOS,
  Windows and Linux, signing, installers and disk images.
- [Auto-updates](updates.md): signed updates from GitHub releases, an S3
  bucket, your own server or the app's own update service, delta updates,
  and an update window in the manner of Sparkle.
- [GitHub Actions](github-actions.md): a workflow that builds, signs and
  notarizes the apps of every platform, and publishes them with their
  updates, when you push a tag.

## Official plugins

- [Fetch](plugins/fetch.md): a `fetch` that makes HTTP requests from Go,
  with no CORS, any header, streamed bodies and cancellation.
- [WebSocket](plugins/websocket.md): a `WebSocket` whose connections Go
  makes, with headers on the handshake.
- [SQLite](plugins/sqlite.md): local databases with parameterized queries
  and atomic transactions, without cgo.
- [Watch](plugins/watch.md): changes to files, in the directories the app
  lets pages watch.
- [Updater](plugins/updater.md): an update window in the manner of
  Sparkle, which checks for updates and offers to install them.
- [Terminal](plugins/terminal.md): a terminal for native UI, which runs
  the shell or any program with Ghostty's terminal emulator.
- [Glass](plugins/glass.md): Liquid Glass for native UI, as macOS draws
  it, on every platform, with macOS's scroll edges and backdrop blurs.
- [Game](plugins/game.md): what games need beyond what apps do, opt-in:
  a game loop in fixed steps with its input, a camera, and gamepads in
  one standard layout.
- [Loading](plugins/loading.md): loading.dev's 29 loading indicators for
  native UI.
- [SF Symbols](plugins/sfsymbols.md): Apple's SF Symbols for native UI on
  macOS, drawn by the system.
- [Automation](plugins/automation.md): drive a running app from another
  process, as end-to-end test runners and agents do: its windows,
  elements, input, menus and screenshots, and `mygo-automation`, its
  command line client for agents.
- [PermissionFlow](plugins/permissionflow.md): the system's permissions,
  such as Accessibility and Screen Recording, checked and asked for, and a
  guide to System Settings with the app to drag into its list.

## Reference

- [Configuration](configuration.md): `mygo.config.ts`, or `mygo.json`.
- [The mygo CLI](cli.md): its commands and flags.
- The Go API: `go doc -all github.com/egoist/mygo`, with the documentation
  of every type and method.
- [Architecture](architecture.md): how MyGo works inside, for contributors,
  with a table of the differences between platforms.

## Requirements

To develop apps you need [Go](https://go.dev/dl/) 1.27 or later and, for
the frontend tooling of projects with a web frontend,
[Bun](https://bun.sh); projects of native UI need Go alone. MyGo uses no
cgo, so there is no C toolchain to install, and any machine can compile the
apps of every platform; signing and disk images of macOS apps need a Mac.

Apps run on:

| Platform | Windows with web pages need | Windows of native UI need |
|---|---|---|
| macOS 12 or later | nothing: WKWebView is part of macOS | nothing: they draw with Metal |
| Linux (x64, arm64) | GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1 (or 4.0): `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0` on Debian and Ubuntu, `webkit2gtk4.1` on Fedora, `webkit2gtk-4.1` on Arch Linux | GTK 3 alone |
| Windows 10 and 11 (x64, arm64) | the [WebView2 Runtime](https://developer.microsoft.com/microsoft-edge/webview2/), which Windows 11 includes | nothing: they draw with Direct3D 11 |

An app whose windows all show native UI needs neither WebKitGTK nor the
WebView2 Runtime. Tray icons on Linux also need `libayatana-appindicator3`.
On Linux, MyGo turns WebKitGTK's DMA-BUF renderer off unless the app opts
in, see [drawing web pages on Linux](app.md#drawing-web-pages-on-linux).

An app that shows web pages can ask whether the machine has a webview with
`mygo.WebViewAvailable()`, also before `App.Run`, and open a window of native UI where it has
none, as the table's last column describes.

`mygo doctor` checks a development machine.

# Native UI

A window can show a user interface that MyGo draws itself instead of a web
page. You write it in Go with package `ui`: there is no HTML, no JavaScript
and no frontend build, and the window starts no webview, so it opens at
once and uses little memory. MyGo draws it on the GPU, with Metal on macOS,
Direct3D 11 on Windows and OpenGL on Linux.

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"log"

	"github.com/egoist/mygo"
	"github.com/egoist/mygo/ui"
)

// counter is the app's state.
type counter struct{ n int }

// view builds the window's interface from the state, for every frame.
func (app *counter) view(c *ui.Context) {
	ui.Column(c).Fill().Center().Gap(12).Children(func() {
		ui.Text(c, fmt.Sprint(app.n)).FontSize(40).Bold()
		if ui.PrimaryButton(c, "Increment").Clicked() {
			app.n++
		}
	})
}

func main() {
	app := &counter{}
	mygo.App.WhenReady(func() {
		mygo.NewWindow(mygo.WindowOptions{
			Title:   "Counter",
			Width:   320,
			Height:  240,
			Content: ui.View(app.view),
		})
	})
	if err := mygo.App.Run(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

**Reading the examples.** The examples in these guides are parts of a view
such as `counter.view`: `c` is the view's `*ui.Context`, and `app` its
receiver, the value of your own type that holds the state. A field such as
`app.volume` or a method such as `app.save()` is one you declare on that
type, as `counter` declares `n`; [Views](views.md) says more.

`mygo init -template native my-app` starts a native UI project (see
[the CLI](../cli.md#mygo-init)). The [counter example](../../examples/counter-native)
includes a view test, and the [gallery](../../examples/gallery) shows the
controls and layouts.


One app can have windows of both kinds. Native UI suits tools, settings,
inspectors and utilities, and apps that must start instantly; a web page
suits rich documents, existing web code and anything that needs what only
a browser has. Screen readers and other assistive technology read native
UI as they read other apps (see [Accessibility](accessibility.md)).

## Guides

- [Views](views.md): build lifetimes, event queries and callbacks, keys,
  and changing the state from other goroutines.
- [Layout](layout.md): rows and columns, sizes, spacing, alignment and
  positioning.
- [Text](text.md): text and its style, rich text, links within sentences,
  and fonts.
- [Styling and themes](styling.md): backgrounds, borders, shadows and
  gradients, and the theme that follows the desktop.
- [Input](input.md): the pointer, the keyboard focus, shortcuts, the keys
  held, input methods, dropped files, and widgets that take every key.
- [Drag and drop](drag-and-drop.md): values dragged within the window, and
  rows reordered by dragging.
- [Pages and navigation](navigation.md): a router of pages with a history,
  layouts, transitions, and going back and forward.
- [Overlays](overlays.md): what dialogs, popovers and the layer above the
  window share: the focus, Escape, and what is behind them.
- [Accessibility](accessibility.md): what screen readers see, naming
  elements, roles, descriptions and announcements.
- [Right to left](right-to-left.md): interfaces laid out from the right
  for Arabic and Hebrew, logical edges, and what mirrors.
- [Languages](../i18n.md#native-ui): the window's language and regional
  formats, numbers and dates written in them, and the controls' own
  strings.
- [Drawing and animation](drawing.md): painting on elements, shaping text,
  and values that ease to their targets.
- [Shaders](shaders.md): pixels computed on the GPU by shaders written in
  Go's syntax, with values and images the app passes them.
- [Transitions](transitions.md): elements that move, resize, recolor and
  shade smoothly as the layout changes, and come and go.
- [Motion](motion.md): springs that keep their velocity, curves, delays,
  values thrown by the pointer, keyframes, timelines that play several
  tweens on one playhead, and knowing when they are done.
- [Transforms](transforms.md): visual translation, scaling and rotation of
  any element, which the pointer, text input and accessibility follow.
- [Custom widgets](custom-widgets.md): the widgets without a look that every
  widget is built on, and widgets of your own.
- [Windows with native UI](windows.md): window options, title bars drawn by
  the view, zooming the content, and vibrancy.
- [Testing](testing.md): running a view without a window, as fast as a unit
  test.
- [Inspector](inspector.md): the elements of a window, their boxes and
  styles, and the time frames take, beside the content.
- [Rendering](rendering.md): how MyGo draws, on the GPU or the CPU.
- [Browsers](browsers.md): the same app in a page, compiled to
  WebAssembly and drawn with WebGL 2.
- [Migration](migration.md): element values, persistent handles, focus
  bindings and source migration.
- [Performance](performance.md): measured frame costs and retained memory.

## Actions

- [Button](button.md): a push button, plain or in the accent color.
- [Link](link.md): text that opens a URL, or a page of a router.
- [Menu button](menu-button.md): a button opening a menu below it, the
  system's or one MyGo draws in the window with the theme's look.
- [Context menu](context-menu.md): a menu of the system's for any element,
  on a right click, or one MyGo draws in the window with the theme's look;
  [every menu of a window](context-menu.md#every-menu-of-a-window) drawn so,
  text inputs' and tables' too.
- [Toggle](toggle.md): a button that stays pressed, and toggles joined in a
  group.
- [Segmented control](segmented.md): segments choosing one of a few views.
- [Toolbar](toolbar.md): a row of controls along a window, which overflow
  into a menu.

## Choices

- [Checkbox](checkbox.md): a check box, and a check box over a group of
  others.
- [Switch](switch.md): a switch that turns a setting on and off.
- [Radio](radio.md): radio buttons choosing one value, in a group.
- [Select](select.md): a drop-down choosing one of a list.
- [Slider](slider.md): a slider setting a value in a range, with or without
  steps.
- [Range slider](range-slider.md): two knobs setting a low and a high value.
- [Stepper](stepper.md): arrows stepping a value up and down.
- [Rating](rating.md): stars setting a rating.

## Text input

- [Text input](text-input.md): text on one line or several, with selection,
  undo, the clipboard and input methods.
- [Text-input primitives](text-input-client.md): application-owned text,
  native composition and queries, and retained geometry for custom controls.
- [Number input](number-input.md): a number in a range, typed or stepped.
- [Decimal input](decimal-input.md): an exact decimal, as an amount of money,
  typed or stepped, never rounded.
- [Search field](search-field.md): a field for searching, which Escape
  clears.
- [Combobox](combobox.md): a field choosing one of a list, which typing
  filters.
- [Autocomplete](autocomplete.md): a text input suggesting what was typed.
- [Token field](token-field.md): a list of strings as chips, as tags or
  recipients.
- [Editable text](editable-text.md): a text renamed in place, as a file's
  name in Finder.
- [Find bar](find-bar.md): a bar for finding text, with the count of
  matches and the next and previous ones.
- [Rich text editor](rich-text-editor.md): attributed text with formats,
  links, headings, lists, tasks and images, the shortcuts and Format menu
  of word processors, rich copy and paste, and Markdown.

## Code

- [Code editor](code-editor.md): an editor of code as Zed's, with
  highlighting, several carets, folding, completions and diagnostics, for
  files of any size.
- [Diff viewer](diff-viewer.md): the changes between two texts, side by
  side or unified, with the new text editable and changes to review.

## Documents

- [Markdown](markdown.md): CommonMark and GitHub's Markdown, as finished
  documents or a language model's replies streaming in, selectable and
  copied as text or Markdown.

## Dates and colors

- [Calendar](calendar.md): a month choosing a day.
- [Date input](date-input.md): a date in a field, chosen in a calendar below
  it.
- [Time input](time-input.md): the time of day, its hours and minutes typed
  or stepped.
- [Color picker](color-picker.md): a color well, and the picker it opens.

## Collections

- [List](list.md): rows of any number and height, built only while in view.
- [Table](table.md): rows in columns that the user sorts, resizes and moves.
- [Tree](tree.md): items that open and close, built inside the items they
  belong to.
- [Outline](outline.md): a tree of any size, as a list or a table.
- [Grid view](grid-view.md): items in a grid of any size, as a photo
  library.

## Containers

- [Scroll view](scroll.md): containers that scroll their children.
- [Grid](grid.md): children in columns and rows, as CSS grid lays them out.
- [Split view](split.md): two panes with a divider the user drags.
- [Collapsible](collapsible.md): content that a label shows and hides.
- [Accordion](accordion.md): sections that open and close, one above the
  other.
- [Form](form.md): labeled controls with descriptions and errors.
- [Web view](web-view.md): a web page in the window, under the native UI
  painted after it, as menus and dialogs.

## Navigation

- [Tabs](tabs.md): a row of tabs choosing a page.
- [Sidebar](sidebar.md): a source list of items in sections, as Finder's.
- [Breadcrumbs](breadcrumbs.md): a path whose items take the user back.
- [Back and forward buttons](history-buttons.md): buttons going through a
  router's history.

## Dialogs and messages

- [Dialog](dialog.md): a dialog over the dimmed window.
- [Alert dialog](alert-dialog.md): a question about something important,
  with buttons.
- [Popover](popover.md): a panel below an element.
- [Tooltip](tooltip.md): a tip shown as the pointer rests on an element, or
  the keyboard focus comes to it.
- [Toast](toast.md): a short message near the bottom of the window, with an
  action or not.

## Status

- [Progress bar](progress.md): work done so far, or of unknown length.
- [Spinner](spinner.md): spokes turning while work of unknown length goes
  on.
- [Meter](meter.md): a value in a range, colored by its level.
- [Badge](badge.md): a short text in a pill, as a count.

## Charts

- [Charts](chart.md): scales, axes and marks without a look, for bars,
  lines, areas, stacks and donuts, and a selection the pointer and the
  keyboard move.

## Images

- [Image](image.md): bitmaps and SVGs in their own colors.
- [Video](video.md): video files and streams with sound, played by the
  system's media engine, and animated GIFs and PNGs, as trailers, clips
  behind the content or previews.
- [Icon](icon.md): SVG icons in the color of the text.
- [Avatar](avatar.md): a picture of a person, or their initials.
